plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by the ascending clock exit points. In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it neither costs you when you'd lose anyway (bidding higher just risks overpaying) nor forgoes profitable wins (bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities). Since my value is $31, I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

Since the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid (not their own bid), this mirrors a second-price/Vickrey auction. Bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying, since I only pay less than my bid if I win. Bidding below value risks losing profitable wins; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $46.

This auction mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price only determines when I drop out. Since I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid (as long as I'm the highest), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit by ensuring I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own.
